subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
subcategory: Privacy Laws That Changed the World
title: China's Privacy Paradox
description: A quick, practical guide to China's Privacy Paradox.

hook.text: China passed one of the world's strictest data privacy laws — then exempted the government completely.

buildup.text: The Personal Information Protection Law, effective 2021, imposes GDPR-like rules on companies handling data.

discovery.text: It requires consent, limits data collection, and imposes heavy fines on companies that violate user rights.

twist.text: The government itself runs mass surveillance, facial recognition, and the social credit system — all exempt.

climax.text: China protects citizens from corporate data abuse while conducting the most extensive state surveillance on Earth.

punchline.text: Protected from companies. Watched by the state.

quiz.question: What makes China's privacy law paradoxical?
options: It restricts corporate data use while the government conducts mass surveillance
It only applies to foreign companies
